data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 argues the large service wins by positing two separate mechanisms (centralized patching and coordination complexity), but the patch-latency claim has no demonstrated causal link to correlated failure. Unpatched nodes being 'weakest links' that 'cascade' through API calls actually shows correlated failure spreading in the decentralized network, yet the argument never addresses the symmetric mechanism for the large service: a single logic bug in core code is replicated across every redundant node, so the patch reaches all nodes instantly but the failure reaches all nodes instantly too. By assuming the large service's redundancy is not all running identical code, the argument suppresses the very correlated failure mode that makes replicated redundancy fragile, so the causal mechanism is incomplete relative to the problem.
